Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Treat those dimensions as targets, not as permission to ignore the wall framing or the space available for the table to swing open.

The floor is concrete and slightly uneven. There is a clear area in front of the wall, but a marked aisle must remain open; the table cannot project into that aisle when folded up. Explain how the mounting arrangement can transfer the load into the framing, and identify any measurements that must be checked at the actual site before cutting parts.

Available shop equipment includes a circular saw with a straightedge guide, a jigsaw, a drill/driver, ordinary clamps, a random-orbit sander, and common hand tools. The makerspace has a track saw, but it must be reserved, so the instructions should not depend on it. Available lumber includes construction-grade 2-by-4s and 3/4-inch plywood. The plywood sheets are 4 by 8 feet. Some of the framing lumber may be bowed or twisted, so include a simple way to inspect stock and explain where a straight piece matters most. No hardwood, specialty table hardware, welding, or permanent alteration to the concrete floor is available.

Please keep the design suitable for a volunteer-run space where several people may use it and where the builder may have only one weekend to complete the work. Use commonly available folding-leg brackets or another clearly described, commercially available support method; do not rely on a custom metal fabrication. If more than one reasonable hardware option exists, describe the trade-off briefly and give one practical default without claiming it is the only safe choice. Make clear that the selected brackets and fasteners must be rated for the intended load and compatible with the actual installation. 5. A final inspection and first-use check, including how to look for movement at the wall, rocking on the uneven floor, binding hardware, and a tabletop that is not acceptably flat.

Do not suggest attaching the table to the concrete floor.

The tone should be clear and practical, not promotional. Avoid claiming that the design is guaranteed safe or suitable for every shop.
